replicated_originals.reference: Cornelissen, Bester, Cairns, Tovée & Cornelissen (2015) The influence of personal BMI on body size estimations and sensitivity to body size change in anorexia spectrum disorders
Cornelissen, McCarty, Cornelissen & Tovée (2017) Body size estimation in women with anorexia nervosa and healthy controls using 3D avatars

A.reason: Ref 18; the paper states it 'serves both as a replication and extension of Cornelissen et al. [17,18]', aiming to replicate the group difference in the regression slope of self-estimated BMI on actual BMI (ED group vs controls).

B.reason: Ref 20, cited only within [19–25] as prior evidence of contraction bias in healthy individuals; not one of the studies the paper names as its replication targets.

C.reason: Ref 17; the primary replication target — the sample size, 3:1 control:ANSD design and power analysis follow Cornelissen et al. [17], and the BMI-by-group interaction it reported is the tested effect.

notes: Self-replication by the same lab, using a method-of-adjustment task in place of the original yes/no task, better-matched BMI ranges, and an added SATAQ. Refs 17 and 18 are always cited together as the replicated originals; ref 17 is the main one for design and power.
